title: Elephants, Rhinos and Their Conservation Projects

cards.b:
UPSC likes species projects: which year, which animal, which state. Elephant and rhino are also common in current affairs because of human-wildlife conflict and poaching.

This lesson gives the key dates and numbers.

Expect questions that link species with their status on the IUCN list and with the right Schedule of the WPA.

Project Elephant was launched in 1992 to protect elephants, their habitat and corridors, and to address conflict. It is run by the MoEFCC. India has about 33 elephant reserves in over 14 states. The Asian elephant is Endangered (IUCN) and in Schedule I of the WPA.

The Government declared the elephant a National Heritage Animal in 2010, after the Elephant Task Force (2010) report Gajah. World Elephant Day is 12 August.

The 2017 census counted about 27,312 elephants. Karnataka had the most, followed by Assam and Kerala. A later DNA-based count in 2025 reported a lower figure (verify before using). India holds over half of all wild Asian elephants.

Habitat patches are shrinking. Over 400 people a year are killed in conflict across India (government figures, recent years), and elephants die from train hits, electric fences and poisoning. Rail corridors in Assam and Odisha are black spots.

An elephant corridor is a strip of land that links two forests. India has over 100 identified corridors. Wildlife Trust of India and the MoEFCC published a report on them. Some are on private land, so their protection needs state action. Underpasses and speed limits on trains help. A mother herd roams hundreds of square kilometres.

The Indian rhino is Vulnerable (IUCN) and Schedule I. It is found mostly in Kaziranga (Assam), also in Pobitora, Orang and Manas, and in Jaldapara and Gorumara in West Bengal. Kaziranga is a World Heritage Site (1985). The population in India is about 4,000, over 2,600 in Assam.

The Indian Rhino Vision 2020 was a plan from 2005 to reach 3,000 rhinos in Assam by translocation. Poaching for horn is the main threat. Rhinos are also flood-prone.

The Javan rhino (Critically Endangered) lives only in Ujung Kulon in Indonesia. The Sumatran rhino is also Critically Endangered. The white and black rhinos are African. Two African rhino species are mixed up in questions with the Indian one. The Asian rhinos have one or two horns; African rhinos have two.

Ivory and horn trade is still a threat, but the larger long-term threat is habitat loss. Compensation and conflict are huge. Some states allow chilli fences, bee fences and early-warning SMS. Critics say translocation of "problem" elephants to captivity or zoos is cruel. Temples and mahouts raise the issue of captive elephants.

The Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 bans hunting and trade. Project Elephant and the Elephant reserve model are administrative. The Supreme Court (2020) upheld the Nilgiris elephant corridor near Mudumalai. Karnataka and Kerala have railways limiting speeds on elephant tracks. The MIKE programme (Monitoring the Illegal Killing of Elephants) is a CITES tool.

• Project Elephant: 1992. Heritage Animal: 2010.
  • Elephant reserves: about 33.
  • Census 2017: 27,312.
  • Rhino: Kaziranga, Vulnerable.
  • World Elephant Day: 12 Aug.

Tiger, elephant, rhino, lion and leopard are all Schedule I species. Their reserves and census cycles are often paired in one question. The 2017 census total of 27,312 is the figure most questions use.

Prelims-style: "Project Elephant was launched in" (1992). "Which state holds the highest elephant population?" (Karnataka in 2017).

Mains-style: "Why is human-elephant conflict rising and what can be done?" Structure: causes (habitat loss, corridors, crop raids); impact; policy (Project Elephant, corridors); local solutions; way forward.

Add one local solution, such as early-warning systems in Assam or honey-bee fences in Karnataka, to lift a Mains answer. A Prelims favourite is the pairing of project and year, so write each pair down.

quiz.w: It is a centrally sponsored scheme.
